seoTitle: Free UUID v5 and v3 Name-Based Generator
metaDescription: Generate deterministic name-based UUIDs v5 (SHA-1) or v3 (MD5) from a namespace and names, one per line. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Pick a namespace and list names, and get name-based UUIDs. Version 5 uses SHA-1 and version 3 uses MD5, so the same name always gives the same UUID.
why:
Random UUIDs are good for new records, but sometimes you need the same identifier every time you see the same thing: a URL, a domain name, an email address, a product code. Name-based UUIDs solve this, because they are computed from a namespace and a name rather than chosen at random.

They let different systems produce matching ids for imported data without sharing a lookup table. The built-in namespaces are DNS, URL, OID and X500, or you can supply your own UUID. Version 5 is preferred over 3 because SHA-1 beats MD5, although neither is a security feature. Do not use these ids to hide or protect private values.
howTo: Choose version 5 or 3, and a namespace such as DNS or URL.
Enter one name per line. Use a custom namespace UUID if you have your own.
Copy the UUIDs, each listed with the name it came from.

faq.a: The UUID is a hash of the namespace bytes followed by the name. The same namespace, name and version always produce the same value, on any machine or language.

faq.q: Should I pick v5 or v3?
faq.a: Use v5 unless you must match an existing v3 id. Both are just ways of hashing names; SHA-1 in v5 is the newer choice, and neither one is for secrets.
Yes. The name is hashed exactly as typed, so Example.com and example.com give different UUIDs. Normalise case before hashing if you want them to match.

faq.q: Does it need a valid custom namespace?
faq.a: Yes. A custom namespace must be a full UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 format, or the tool shows an error instead of generating a result.
